summary: Independent review of the off-session restart-evidence grading fix. OPERATIONAL TOOLING ONLY; no trading code, no runtime path, no deploy needed. THE PROBLEM IT FIXES IS REAL AND WAS FOUND BY USE: the checklist graded a Saturday restart as FAILED because no adjacent live-bar pair bracketed it — on a weekend there are no bars to bracket anything. THE FIX IS THE RIGHT SHAPE AND THIS IS THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST: it replaces a hand-rolled 4 <= local_start.hour < 20 with is_fillable_et_session(restart, 4, 20), the SAME helper the v2 entry window and the OMS exit fillable-session gate already use, which is weekday-and-non-holiday aware. One session model instead of two. A second, private notion of 'is the market open' inside a health tool is exactly how two subsystems drift apart, and if that shared helper is ever wrong we have far larger problems than a checklist. THE SAFETY HALF REMAINS UNCONDITIONAL, which I checked rather than assumed: a bar gap SPANNING the restart still fails in or out of session — 'if spanning: failures.append(...)' is not guarded by the session flag. Off-session only relaxes the 'prove live bars bracketed the restart' requirement, which is unsatisfiable when no bars exist. That is the correct thing to relax and the correct thing to keep. MUTATIONS: inverting the session classification turns 6 controls red; forcing everything to be treated as off-session turns 2 red including test_report_requires_bar_brackets_during_a_weekday_market_session. So the classifier itself is pinned in both directions. TWO MUTANTS SURVIVED AND I INVESTIGATED THEM RATHER THAN REPORTING THEM AS GAPS: removing 'spanning == 0' from bar_ok, and requiring brackets even off-session, each leave all 33 tests green. The reason is that bar_ok DOES NOT DRIVE THE VERDICT — the 'failures' list does, and a spanning gap appends to it independently of bar_ok. Those mutations change only the PASS/FAIL text displayed on one table row. They are display-only divergences, not safety holes. FINDING, MINOR AND NON-BLOCKING: the rule is nevertheless expressed TWICE — bar_ok recomputes what the failures branches already decide — so the two can drift, and a drift would print PASS on the Bar-continuity row while the run correctly exits non-zero. Deriving the row status from the failures list instead of recomputing it would remove the duplication and the drift. Worth one commit later; it cannot produce a false overall PASS today. 33 focused tests pass. Controlled full unit pair vs base 2f35bc03: base 46 failed / 3735 passed, head 46 failed / 3743 passed, ZERO new failure names and ZERO fixed, base worktree existence verified before trusting the comparison. Ancestor PASS. Reviewer differs from the author. No blocking findings.
